contract.reader: A C programmer who has read entries 1 and 2 and wants to use several cores on one problem
contract.problem: Making a loop faster on several cores without making it wrong, and knowing why a correct parallel loop can still be slow
contract.outcome: Use OpenMP parallel loops, data-sharing clauses and reductions; find and remove data races; explain x86 TSO and C11 release/acquire; estimate barrier, lock and false-sharing costs; choose a schedule
contract.contribution: Each failure mode shown happening on the reference machine (lost increments, store-buffering reorderings, a 21-fold false-sharing penalty, static-schedule imbalance) and then removed
contract.evidence: Measured programs with output; C18, OpenMP 5.2, Lamport, Adve and Gharachorloo, Sewell et al., Hennessy and Patterson, McCalpin, Williams et al.
contract.limitations: One x86 machine, so weak memory models are described but not measured; OpenMP tasks out of scope

findings.problem: Litmus output lines are wider than the code box at 1280 px; the count for outcome 1,1 is cut
findings.whyItMatters: A reader checking the four outcomes cannot see the full row without discovering the sideways scroll
findings.action: Print the counts on two lines or drop the repeated label so each line fits at 1280 px
findings.acceptance: All four counts of each litmus line visible at 1280 px
